title: Adjectives: colors, sizes, and endings that follow along
title_target: В магазине одежды — V magazine odezhdy
goal: Describe things and people — color, size, character — while mastering adjectives, whose endings must match the noun they describe.
bekal: put adjectives in the masculine, feminine, neuter, and plural
shop for clothes: try things on, ask for another size
use какой / какая / какое to ask "what kind"

dialogs.title: Диалог — Looking for a winter coat
dialogs.intro: Ani doesn't have a warm enough coat yet. Даша goes to the store with her. Notice how every adjective changes its ending to match the noun after it.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Yes, I'm looking for a warm coat.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Black or gray. Nothing too bright.
lines.literal: black — or — gray. not — very — bright.

lines.speaker: Даша:
lines.id: Why not red? Winter is gray, you'll stand out.
lines.literal: and — why — not — red (n)? winter — gray (f), you — will-be — bright (f).

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Hmm… Can I try on the red one?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I don't know. Sizes are different in Indonesia.
lines.literal: not — know. in — Indonesia — other — sizes.

lines.speaker: Продавщица:
lines.id: Probably a forty-four. The fitting room is over there.

lines.speaker: Даша:
lines.id: Great! Red coat, black bag, black boots. You're a real Muscovite.
lines.literal: great! red — coat, black (f) — bag, black (pl) — boots. you — real — Muscovite (f).

notes: **Adjectives must match their noun.** ⚠️ In English "red" never changes: red scarf, red bag, red boots. In Russian it changes three times: *красн**ый** шарф* (masc), *красн**ая** сумка* (fem), *красн**ое** пальто* (neut), *красн**ые** сапоги* (pl). The noun decides, and the adjective always comes **before it**, just like in English.

**The endings are neat and easy to spot:** masculine **-ый / -ий / -ой**, feminine **-ая**, neuter **-ое**, plural **-ые / -ие**. If you can name the noun's gender (Unit 2), you can choose the adjective ending.

**The masculine ending -ой is always stressed.** *больш**ой***, *плох**ой***, *друг**ой***, *как**ой***. Compare *нов**ый*** and *красн**ый***, which are stressed on the root. The tell: if the ending is -ой, the stress is right there.

**Какой isn't just "which," it's also "what kind."** *Какой у вас размер?* (what's your size?), *Какая погода?* (what's the weather like?), *Какое пальто?* (what kind of coat?). It changes its own ending to match the noun, just like any other adjective.

**Пальто never changes form.** Loanwords from French ending in -о stay frozen in every case: *в пальто*, *без пальто*, *красное пальто*. The same goes for **кафе**, **метро**, **такси**, **кино**, **радио**. A pleasant little group.

**Вам помочь? is the standard line of Russian shop assistants.** Literally "to-you help?" The answer: *Да, спасибо* or *Нет, спасибо, я просто смотрю* (no thanks, I'm just looking). ⚠️ Anyone who hates being followed around by sales staff should learn that last line.
**Ну is the most common filler word in everyday Russian.** It means "well," "so," "yeah," depending on the tone. *Ну как?* — well? how is it? *Ну ладно* — oh well, OK.

grammars.title: Adjective endings
body: Four endings for four types. Look at the noun, pick the ending.
after: ⚠️ After **г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ**, the letter **ы** can't be written and is replaced by **и**: хорош**ий**, хорош**ие**, больш**ие**, русск**ий**, русск**ие**. This spelling rule applies across all of Russian, not just adjectives. Memorize those seven letters — they'll come up again and again.
Adjectives also change by case (*в больш**ом** доме*), but that's beyond A1. For now the nominative is enough — the form used when the noun is the subject or stands alone.

grammars.title: Colors
body: All colors are adjectives, so they all change their endings. They're listed below in the masculine form.
after: ⚠️ Russian treats **синий** (dark blue) and **голубой** (light blue) as two separate colors, not two shades of one color. English doesn't make this split, and research shows Russian speakers really do tell the two apart faster than speakers of other languages. The sky is голубой; the deep sea is синий.
**Синий** follows the soft adjective pattern, so its feminine is **синяя** and its neuter **синее**, not синая/синое.

blocks.title: Ready-made phrases for the clothing store
items: **Можно примерить?** — Can I try it on?
**Есть размер побольше / поменьше?** — Do you have a bigger / smaller size?
**Есть другой цвет?** — Do you have another color?
**Мне велико / Мне мало.** — It's too big / too small for me.

⚠️ Russian clothing sizes use European numbers (42, 44, 46 …), and shoes use their own scale, which can **differ** from US and UK sizes and even slightly from EU sizes. Being off by one size is common. Always try things on first.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of красный.
Fill in the form of большой or хороший that matches the word in parentheses.
Put the words in the right order.

items: I'm looking for a warm coat.
A black bag and black boots.
Do you have a bigger size?

answers: красный — красная — красное — красные — красная — красное
большой — большая — хорошая — хороший — большое — хорошие
Я ищу тёплое пальто. — Какой цвет вы хотите? — Можно примерить? — Какой у вас размер? — Я просто смотрю.
